Almost all of Jacksonville's fantasy options disappointed in this matchup, but they should be able to bounce back in a competitive matchup against the Eagles next week.

news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 19-of-29 passing attempts for 182 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception while adding 25 yards on the ground in Sunday's 35-6 blowout win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Trevor Lawrence tosses three touchdowns in blowout win Sunday
news.impact: Lawrence played a stellar game on Sunday, finishing with over 200 total yards and three touchdowns in a big win over the Patriots. He has been playing well so far this season and will continue to be a viable starting option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 17 of his 29 passes for 189 yards and an interception while adding six yards on two rushes in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.head: Trevor Lawrence throws for 189 yards in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Lawrence got the Jaguars off to a fast start as they were leading 10-3 at halftime, but the Broncos came to life on defense starting in the third quarter. Lawrence has now thrown for 434 yards and four touchdowns through the first two games of the season. He will be a solid QB1 in fantasy in Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns. He also ran twice for three yards.
news.head: Trevor Lawrence flawless in big win over Browns
news.impact: Lawrence played on easy mode against a Browns defense that just couldn't create stops. He had only five incompletions to four touchdowns on the day, a great ratio to have. With their win over the Browns, the Jags are the only AFC South team to clinch a win on Sunday. He faces a much tougher test against the Broncos next week.

news.body: Tyler Shough completed 30-of-48 passing attempts for 286 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: Tyler Shough throws for 286 yards in loss Monday
news.impact: New Orleans had a rough game on Monday night, suffering a blowout loss at the hands of their divisional rivals at home. Shough was personally able to have an okay game, however, logging close to 300 total yards and taking good care of the ball over the course of the night. Fantasy managers probably aren't satisfied with his output in this game, but he should bounce back and return to having high value sometime within the next game or two.

news.body: Tyler Shough completed 29-of-42 passes for 255 yards with four touchdowns and one interception in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday.
news.head: Tyler Shough throws four touchdowns, struggles with turnovers late
news.impact: Shough was dealing through the first three quarters, tossing four touchdowns with two of them going to Juwan Johnson and the other two going to Noah Fant. The Saints turned the ball over four times in the fourth quarter with three of them being committed by Shough on an interception and two fumbles. He'll face the Falcons next week.

news.body: Tyler Shough completed 27-of-34 passes for 252 yards and one touchdown in a 24-17 win over the Ravens.
news.head: Tyler Shough executes late comeback win in Week 2
news.impact: Shough also added 23 rushing yards on nine carries in the win. Both of the second-year quarterback's touchdowns came in the fourth quarter to tie the game and give the Saints the lead. Shough has looked great through his first two games of the season and will look to build on these performances in a Week 3 matchup with Las Vegas.

news.body: Tyler Shough completed 35-of-56 pass attempts for 410 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions while also rushing four times for eight yards in the Saints' 31-30 Week 1 overtime loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Tyler Shough electrifies late in Week 1 loss to Lions
news.impact: Shough carried the New Orleans offense late in the contest after trailing 21-0 at one point, throwing three second-half touchdowns to force overtime in the Week 1 loss. The second-year signal-caller faces a stiff test in Week 2 against a tough Baltimore Ravens defense next.

news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. rushed the ball 20 times for 94 yards and caught 4-of-8 targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. totals 128 yards Sunday
news.impact: The veteran played well on Sunday. He logged 128 total yards against the Dolphins, and he was able to do that while maintaining good efficiency. He will continue to be a worthwhile fantasy option for however long Jordan Mason (thumb) remains out of the lineup for the Vikings.

news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. ran for 58 yards on 17 carries in the Vikings 23-16 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday. He also caught 5-of-6 targets for 34 yards receiving.
news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. totals 22 touches Sunday
news.impact: It wasn't the most efficient performance for Jones, but his overall volume made up for it. He'll be an RB2 play next week against the Dolphins.

news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Jones was able to return to practice to finish the week. He should remain an RB2 play in a lead role in the Vikings backfield.

news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. practiced again on Friday.
news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) practices Friday
news.impact: Jones was limited in his return to practice on Thursday. He should be in line for another lead role on Sunday against the Buccaneers. He'll be an RB2 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Alvin Kamara rushed the ball seven times for 23 yards and two touchdowns while adding five receptions for 35 yards on the ground in Monday's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: Alvin Kamara scores twice in loss Monday
news.impact: Kamara suffered an injury of some kind in the middle of Monday night's game, but he was able to return and finish out the contest. He ended up finishing with a good fantasy total thanks to his two touchdowns and five receptions on the night, though he wasn't where the team needed him to be in terms of efficiency. He will continue to be a worthwhile fantasy asset for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Alvin Kamara ran for 36 yards on nine carries in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday. He also caught his lone target for five yards receiving.
news.head: Alvin Kamara sees nine carries Sunday
news.impact: Kamara saw his role expand after Travis Etienne Jr. left the game early. He'll be in the flex conversation next week if Etienne is sidelined.

news.body: Alvin Kamara rushed for 15 yards on nine carries in the Saints' 24-17 win over the Ravens. He caught 5-of-6 targets for seven yards.
news.head: Alvin Kamara hauls in five passes in Week 2 win
news.impact: Kamara was very limited in his production in his 2026 debut, was clearly a focal point of the offense which cut into Travis Etienne's volume. Fantasy managers will want to be cautious with both running backs volume in question heading into a Week 3 matchup with Las Vegas.

news.body: Alvin Kamara is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
news.head: Alvin Kamara (knee) off injury report for Week 2
news.impact: Kamara will be good to go for his season debut. He should be in a third down/passing down role in the Saints backfield behind Travis Etienne.

news.body: Ashton Jeanty carried the ball 15 times for 58 yards and caught six of his eight targets for 68 yards in a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs in Week 4.
news.head: Ashton Jeanty runs for 58 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Jeanty salvaged another tough day on the ground with his work in the passing game. He briefly left the game with what appeared to be an ankle injury but was able to return to action, although it is concerning considering he has been dealing with an ankle issue since the preseason. The second-year running back has been held to 58 or fewer rushing yards in three straight games but continues to see the majority of the backfield work in Las Vegas. He will be a solid RB1 in Week 5 vs. the Patriots.

news.body: Ashton Jeanty ran for 56 yards on 19 carries in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints. He also caught 3-of-3 targets for 36 yards receiving.
news.head: Ashton Jeanty struggles on ground Sunday
news.impact: Jeanty was inefficient on the ground for the second straight week. He still remained active in the passing game. He remains an RB1 in a workhorse role moving forward.

news.body: Ashton Jeanty rushed the ball 21 times for 48 yards and caught 4-of-7 targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Ashton Jeanty inefficient in win Sunday
news.impact: Jeanty didn't look great on Sunday. He totaled just 63 on his 28 opportunities against the Chargers, and he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all, which left him with an underwhelming fantasy total. The Raiders have a tough schedule coming up, so the young running back will need to step up his game if he wants to deliver for fantasy managers.

news.body: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
news.head: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) logs full practice Wednesday
news.impact: Jeanty seems to be entirely over his ankle injury at this point, as he played through it in Week 1 and now logs a full practice session to start the week on Wednesday. He should be a full go and high-quality fantasy option moving forward, assuming he suffers no setbacks with his recovery.

news.body: Bhayshul Tuten rushed the ball 17 times for 73 yards and caught two passes for 18 yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Bhayshul Tuten racks up 91 yards in win Sunday
news.impact: Tuten had a good game on Sunday, finishing as the team's top rusher and dominating the touches in the backfield en route to a win over the Bengals. Chris Rodriguez Jr. was the one to get into the end zone for the Jaguars, however, which was annoying for fantasy managers to see. The young running back should continue to be a worthwhile fantasy asset moving forward.

news.body: Bhayshul Tuten rushed the ball 15 times for 73 yards and caught two passes for 17 yards in Sunday's 35-6 win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Bhayshul Tuten leads team in rushing Sunday
news.impact: Tuten had a good game on Sunday. He led the team in rushing yards at an efficient clip of 4.9 yards per carry, and he was also able to get into the end zone at one point, which left him with a great fantasy total. He should again be started in a matchup against the Bengals next week.

news.body: Bhayshul Tuten carried the ball 13 times for 65 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for minus-three yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.head: Bhayshul Tuten finds the end zone in Week 2
news.impact: Tuten punched in a one-yard touchdown in the second quarter to give the Jaguars an early 7-0 lead. The second-year back also vastly outproduced Chris Rodriguez Jr., who had just 13 yards on six carries. Tuten has now racked up 131 rushing yards through two games. He will be a solid RB2 in fantasy heading into Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.body: Bhayshul Tuten ran 15 times for 66 yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also caught his only target for 22 yards.
news.head: Bhayshul Tuten racks up 66 yards on the ground in win
news.impact: Tuten led the Jags in rushing attempts in the win, but didn't have much to show in terms of fantasy scoring in half- or full-PPR formats. But to be fair, he was efficient in his touches, and it's likely that better days are ahead for the apparent Jags RB1.

news.body: Bijan Robinson rushed the ball 19 times for 145 yards and two touchdowns in Monday night's 45-24 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Bijan Robinson dominant in blowout win Monday
news.impact: Robinson was absolutely dominant on Monday night. He led the Falcons in rushing with 145 yards on the night at a hyper-efficient clip of 7.6 yards per carry, and he was also able to get into the end zone on two separate occasions. He let a little to be desired in the passing game, but that was simply because the Falcons were up so much for so long. He has been stellar over the first four weeks of the season and should continue to be one of the best assets in all of fantasy moving forward.

news.body: Bijan Robinson ran 29 times for 194 yards and two touchdowns and caught both of his targets for 19 yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
news.head: Bijan Robinson explodes in Week 3 win over Packers
news.impact: Robinson had his way with the Packers' defense, rushing for 6.7 yards per carry. He ripped off a huge 55-yard gain early on in the game, which opened the floodgates for many more big runs throughout the game. The Packers simply could not stop him, and once the ground game got going, QB Michael Penix and WR Drake London were able to carve up the Packers' secondary. With Penix back, the offense has new life, and Bijan stands to benefit greatly from it, even if Brian Robinson Jr. spells him.

news.body: Bijan Robinson ran 16 times for 72 yards and caught three of four targets for nine yards in the Falcons' 34-3 blowout loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
news.head: Bijan Robinson held in check in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Robinson was fine on the ground, 4.5 yards per carry, but still largely held in check. The Panthers didn't allow the Falcons to move the ball, mostly thanks to Atlanta's lack of competent QB play. If Michael Penix returns on Thursday, that will hopefully be a huge boost to Bijan's value. If not, it's looking like another long night for Bijan managers.

news.body: Bijan Robinson carried the ball 21 times for 83 yards and caught eight of his 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1.
news.head: Bijan Robinson hauls in touchdown catch in Week 1
news.impact: Robinson was basically the entire offense for the Falcons in the close loss to Pittsburgh. He scored the team's only touchdown on a 23-yard catch at the end of the first quarter. It was an excellent start to the season for the star running back, who will slot in as a high-end RB1 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Panthers.

news.body: Blake Corum rushed the ball five times for 14 yards and caught one pass for seven yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Blake Corum a non-factor in win Sunday
news.impact: Corum didn't play much of a role for the Rams in Week 4. He saw just six touches over the course of the game and was only able to turn them into 21 yards, as opposed to Kyren Williams' 26 touches for 147 yards. Fantasy managers shouldn't have much hope for Corum to have standalone value anytime soon.

news.body: Blake Corum rushed the ball six times for 15 yards and caught 2-of-4 targets for zero yards in Sunday's 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Blake Corum quiet in loss Sunday
news.impact: Corum wasn't able to contribute much on Sunday. He totaled just 15 yards on his ten opportunities over the course of the night, which left him with a very poor fantasy total. He will continue to see a good amount of work in Los Angeles' offense moving forward but will likely continue to fall behind Kyren Williams in competitive matchups.

news.body: Blake Corum rushed the ball 12 times for 79 yards and caught one pass for 13 yards in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.head: Blake Corum totals 92 yards in win Monday
news.impact: Los Angeles' offense looked great on Monday night, and Corum was no exception to that. He put up 92 total yards on just 13 opportunities, although he wasn't able to get into the endzone to put the capstone on that. The Rams' backfield is a situation to continue monitoring, with Corum and Kyren Williams each seeing the same amount of carries in this blowout win.

news.body: Blake Corum ran 10 times for 54 yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers on Thursday.
news.head: Blake Corum totals 54 yards in loss
news.impact: Corum was solid on the ground at 5.4 a carry, but that was about all he had going for him. Without a touchdown or receiving work to go along with his yardage, it was a disappointing fantasy performance. However, his usage is encouraging; the Rams at least trust him enough that they will split Kyren Williams' workload with Corum. It makes him a top-tier handcuff RB, and one that should be rostered in case anything happens to Kyren.

news.body: Braelon Allen carried the ball 14 times for 59 yards while catching both of his targets for eight yards in a 23-12 loss to the Bears in Week 4.
news.head: Braelon Allen runs for 59 yards in Week 4 loss
news.impact: Allen got all of the backfield touches but wasn't able to do much with them, averaging just 4.2 yards per carry in the loss. With Breece Hall (quad) looking at least another week or two away from returning, Allen should operate as the Jets' lead back again in Week 5 against the Browns.

news.body: Braelon Allen rushed for 14 yards on four carries in the 31-24 loss to the Lions. He caught all three of his targets for three yards.
news.head: Braelon Allen tallies seven touches in Week 3
news.impact: Allen continued to see limited work Sunday, but he could be in line for more touches in Week 4 if Breece Hall (thigh) misses time. Hall was injured late in the game and will likely undergo testing Monday to determine the severity of the injury.

news.body: Braelon Allen rushed five times for seven yards and one touchdown while also catching his only target for eight yards in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
news.head: Braelon Allen reaches end zone in Week 2 loss to Packers
news.impact: Allen made the most of a forgettable performance as part of an underperforming backfield attack Sunday, scoring his first touchdown of the season in a losing effort. The running back remains more of a complementary option behind No. 1 running back Breece Hall for head coach Aaron Glenn, with a favorable Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions up next.

news.body: Braelon Allen carried the ball 10 times for 40 yards and failed to corral his lone target in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
news.head: Braelon Allen sees 10 carres in backup role in Week 1
news.impact: Allen mixed in as the backup behind Breece Hall, who handled 22 carries and caught two passes. The Jets will continue to utilize Allen to spell Hall throughout the season, but the former only has fantasy value as a handcuff for the time being. He will take on the Packers at home in Week 2.

news.body: Breece Hall (quad) ruled out for Week 4.
news.head: Breece Hall (quad) will not play Sunday
news.impact: Hall has not been practicing this week and, as expected, will not play Sunday. Braelon Allen should be the workhorse back for the Jets in a matchup with the Bears.

news.body: Breece Hall remained sidelined from practice on Thursday.
news.head: Breece Hall (quad) misses practice Thursday
news.impact: Hall remains on track to be sidelined on Sunday against the Bears.

news.body: Breece Hall will be sidelined from practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Breece Hall (quad) not practicing Wednesday
news.impact: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Hall is considered week-to-week. He is likely to sit this Sunday.

news.body: Ian Rapoport reports Breece Hall is considered week-to-week with a quad injury.
news.head: Breece Hall (quad) considered week-to-week
news.impact: Hall received “good news after the MRI” he received. Braelon Allen will figure to take over the lead role in the Jets backfield in his absence. He will be in the RB2/flex range for fantasy managers.

news.body: Bucky Irving carried the ball 16 times for 61 yards in a 17-14 loss to the Packers in Week 4.
news.head: Bucky Irving goes for 61 yards in Week 4 loss
news.impact: He was not targeted in the passing game. Irving dealt with a glute injury throughout the week, but he did not seem affected by it during the game. He did watch as fellow running backs Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker both found the end zone in the close loss. Irving has run for 241 yards and one touchdown through four games this season. He will be on the RB2 radar in Week 5 against the Cowboys.

news.body: Bucky Irving is officially good to go for Sunday's game against the Packers.
news.head: Bucky Irving (glute) good to go Sunday
news.impact: Irving sat on the bench for the majority of the fourth quarter last week. He was limited in practice throughout the week and will be good to go on Sunday.

news.body: Bucky Irving (glute) was officially a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Bucky Irving (glute) officially limited Thursday
news.impact: Irving has been limited in two-straight practices to start the week. He's still managing a glute injury, but it looks more likely than not that he will play through it this week. If he's cleared to play heading into the weekend, fantasy managers should have no hesitations starting him in a matchup against the Packers.

news.body: Bucky Irving practiced again on Thursday.
news.head: Bucky Irving (glute) practices Thursday
news.impact: Irving was limited in practice to open the week on Wednesday. He remains on track to be good to go on Sunday.

news.body: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 18 times for 58 yards and caught one pass for eight yards in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
news.head: Cam Skattebo underwhelming in win Sunday
news.impact: New York was able to score 36 points on Sunday, but Skattebo wasn't really able to get in on the action. He totaled just 66 yards on his 19 touches on the day, and he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all. He'll have a good opportunity to bounce back next week in a favorable matchup against the Commanders.

news.body: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 20 times for 60 yards and caught 3-of-4 targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Cam Skattebo totals 100 yards Sunday
news.impact: On Sunday, Skattebo was practically New York's entire offense. He was the team's leader in rushing and receiving yards, and he nearly doubled the yards of the next closest skill-position player. His workload is elite at this point, but he isn't likely to be a strong fantasy option moving forward given how weak this New York offense is looking without QB Jaxson Dart (knee).

news.body: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 12 times for 36 yards and caught four passes for 19 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Cam Skattebo inefficient in loss Monday
news.impact: Skattebo was pretty well bottled up on Monday night. He was only able to rush for 36 yards at an inefficient clip of 3.0 yards per carry, and he didn't add much in the passing game outside of four receptions. New York's offense as a whole was a mess with injuries in this game, but the young running back will have ample opportunities to bounce back with matchups against the Titans and Cardinals coming up over the next two weeks.

news.body: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.head: Cam Skattebo leads team in rushing Sunday
news.impact: Skattebo looked pretty solid in his first game back from an injury that ended his 2025 season early. He led the team in rushing yards and scored a touchdown against the Cowboys, and he was clearly the team's top RB in terms of carries, outnumbering the next closest back three to one in that area. He didn't see a single target or catch over the course of the night, however. If Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy Jr. continue to serve as the team's primary receiving backs, Skattebo's fantasy ceiling could be capped by that on a week-to-week basis.

news.body: Chase Brown rushed the ball nine times for ten yards and hauled in 11 catches for 71 yards in Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: Chase Brown hauls in 11 passes Sunday
news.impact: Brown was very ineffective as a rusher on Sunday, finishing with just ten yards in a loss to the Jaguars. He was able to contribute heavily through the passing game, however, logging 71 yards on a whopping 11 catches. The Bengals may need to lean on him in the passing game again next week with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) both at risk to be sidelined against the Dolphins.

news.body: Chase Brown rushed for 61 yards on 13 carries in a 30-27 loss to the Steelers. He caught both of his targets for eight yards.
news.head: Chase Brown quiet in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Brown saw a season low in rushing attempts and targets. Despite the lower volume against Pittsburgh, fantasy managers should expect Brown to remain the workhorse running back for the Bengals in Week 4 against the Jaguars.

news.body: Chase Brown ran for 80 yards on 20 carries in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday. He also caught 3-of-5 targets for two yards receiving.
news.head: Chase Brown sees 20 carries Sunday
news.impact: Brown did not find the end zone. He ran well, but it was still a fairly quiet day for him overall for fantasy managers. He'll remain an RB1 against the Steelers next week.

news.body: Chase Brown ran for 56 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers. He also caught 5-of-6 targets for 22 yards receiving.
news.head: Chase Brown finds the end zone Sunday
news.impact: Brown did not have the most efficient afternoon, but it still got the job done for fantasy managers. He draws a tougher matchup in Week 2 against the Texans.

news.body: Christian McCaffrey rushed 15 times for 52 yards and a touchdown while catching three of his five targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Christian McCaffrey scores touchdown in win Sunday
news.impact: McCaffrey didn't have his biggest day from a yardage standpoint, but he found the end zone on a one-yard run in the fourth quarter. He finished with 18 touches and remains the clear lead back in San Francisco. McCaffrey remains a must-start option heading into Week 5 against Seattle.

news.body: Christian McCaffrey ran for 75 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries in the 49ers 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. He also caught 4-of-5 targets for 41 yards receiving.
news.head: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone Sunday
news.impact: McCaffrey took over as the clear lead back on Sunday. He found the end zone in the fourth quarter as the Cardinals were making a comeback. He remains a strong RB1 moving forward.

news.body: Christian McCaffrey (rest) did not take part in San Francisco's practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Christian McCaffrey (rest) doesn't practice Wednesday
news.impact: McCaffrey was given Wednesday off as a veteran rest day, which is normal for him at the first practice of the week. He should be a full go for Sunday's game and remains a must-start fantasy option in all league formats for as long as he stays healthy and on the field.

news.body: Christian McCaffrey gained 23 yards on 10 carries and 43 yards on four catches, scoring twice on the ground in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.head: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone twice in Week 2
news.impact: The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Week 2, but McCaffrey did score a pair of one-yard plunges. As usual, the dual-threat back was also active in the passing game. McCaffrey is up to 29 total touches through two games, averaging 4.6 yards per carry and 7.0 yards per reception. The 49ers appear to be capping the 30-year-old's usage a bit, but he's still a clear RB1, particularly in PPR formats, when healthy.

news.body: Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
news.head: Chuba Hubbard delivers big performance Sunday night
news.impact: The Lions' defense could not stop the pass or the run Sunday night. Hubbard turned in his highest rushing total since December 2024 in this contest. The 27-year-old back has now gained more than 200 yards on 39 carries over the last two weeks, proving himself capable of being a workhorse back yet again. Hubbard will return to the field for a matchup with the Eagles in Week 6.

news.body: Chuba Hubbard (rest) was a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Chuba Hubbard (rest) a full participant Thursday
news.impact: Hubbard was able to practice in a full capacity on Thursday, which was the expectation from the start. He should be a full go for Week 4 and remains a must-start fantasy option at this point in the season.

news.body: Chuba Hubbard was back at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Chuba Hubbard (rest) returns to practice Thursday
news.impact: Hubbard got a rest day from practice to open the week on Wednesday. He remains a strong RB2 for fantasy managers.

news.body: Chuba Hubbard (rest) did not take part in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Chuba Hubbard (rest) doesn't practice Wednesday
news.impact: Carolina is making some efforts to limit Hubbard's workload, giving him the day off on Wednesday to recover from any bumps and bruises that he has sustained through the first few weeks of the season. He should be back at practice on Thursday and is expected to be a full go for Sunday night's matchup against the Lions.

news.body: D'Andre Swift carried the ball 15 times for 58 yards while catching both of his targets for 16 yards in a 23-12 win over the Jets in Week 4. He also lost a fumble in the win.
news.head: D'Andre Swift runs for 58 yards in Week 4 win
news.impact: Swift spent some time on the sidelines after losing a fumble, although it is unclear whether he was benched or was dealing with an injury, as he got up slowly while favoring his knee after the play. Either way, he was outplayed by Kyle Monangai, who ran for 146 yards and two touchdowns. A low-end RB2 in fantasy moving forward, Swift will look to bounce back in Week 5 against the Packers.

news.body: D'Andre Swift (knee) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the New York Jets.
news.head: D'Andre Swift (knee) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: Swift was held out of Chicago's practice on Thursday, but he returned to practice as a full participant on Friday and carries no injury designation heading into the weekend. He should be fully good to go for Sunday's game and should be a safe fantasy option against the Jets, though his fantasy upside will likely be limited with Caleb Williams (hamstring) out for another game.

news.body: D'Andre Swift is expected to return to practice on Friday.
news.head: D'Andre Swift (knee) expected to practice Friday
news.impact: Swift was added to the injury report after not practicing on Thursday. Bears coach Ben Johnson said he is optimistic on Swift playing on Sunday.

news.body: D’Andre Swift (knee) was added to the injury for the Chicago Bears and did not practice Thursday according to Ari Meirov.
news.head: D’Andre Swift (knee) does not practice Thursday
news.impact: Swift’s status will need to be monitored during Friday’s practice session, as another missed opportunity could leave the running back’s status in doubt, with Kyle Monangai in line for increased touches in Week 4 if Swift cannot suit up for head coach Ben Johnson.

news.body: David Montgomery ran for 24 yards on 10 carries in the Texans 34-30 loss against the Cowboys.
news.head: David Montgomery shut down Sunday
news.impact: Montgomery continued his recent struggles on the ground. Woody Marks was the running back to find the end zone again. He'll be a low-end RB2/flex play next week against the Titans.

news.body: David Montgomery rushed for 33 yards on 11 carries in a 19-17 loss to the Colts. He caught both targets for 15 yards.
news.head: David Montgomery quiet in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Montgomery continues to struggle, tallying 43 rushing yards on 17 carries over the last two games. The veteran also saw Woody Marks come into the game on a short-yardage touchdown run in the forth quarter. Montgomery and the Texans will take on the Cowboys in Week 4.

news.body: David Montgomery ran for 10 yards on six carries in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught 2-of-2 targets for 14 yards receiving.
news.head: David Montgomery sees just six carries Sunday
news.impact: After a huge Week 1 performance, it was a game to forget for Montgomery and the entire Texans run game. He'll look to bounce back next week against the Colts.

news.body: David Montgomery rushed for 60 yards and two scores on 20 carries, adding three receptions for 19 yards and another touchdown in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.head: David Montgomery has big debut for Texans
news.impact: Montgomery was given 23 touches in his debut with the Texans, as the veteran back was a focal point of the offense. Granted, he only averaged 3.0 yards per carry, but he found the end zone three times while being involved both on the ground and through the air.

news.body: Derrick Henry rushed for 73 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in the Ravens win over the Titans. He caught both of his targets for six yards.
news.head: Derrick Henry finds the end zone in Week 4 win
news.impact: Henry opened the scoring with a five-yard plunge into the end zone in the first quarter. The veteran running back has found the end zone at least once in each of the team's first four games. Fantasy managers should expect Henry to remain a key factor for the Ravens heading into a Week 5 matchup in Atlanta.

news.body: Derrick Henry carried the ball 26 times for 89 yards and two touchdowns while catching his lone target for no gain in a 34-31 win over the Cowboys in Week 3.
news.head: Derrick Henry scores two more TDs in Week 3
news.impact: Henry continued to dominate in the high-scoring win over the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro. The veteran running back punched in scores from three and four yards out in the win, giving him six touchdowns through the first three games of the season. Overall, he's rushed for 301 yards while adding five catches for 38 yards this year. Henry will be a high-end RB1 in Week 4 against the Titans.

news.body: Derrick Henry rushed for 68 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Ravens 24-17 loss to the Saints. He caught all three of his targets for 19 yards.
news.head: Derrick Henry finds the end zone in Week 2
news.impact: Henry found the end zone on a one-yard rush in the first quarter. The veteran was held in check after that, unable to find any big gains on the ground. Henry and the Ravens will take on Dallas in Week 3.

news.body: Derrick Henry carried the ball 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns while also hauling in his lone target for 19 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Derrick Henry rushes for three touchdowns in Week 1 win over Colts
news.impact: Henry capitalized on a sizeable workload out of the Baltimore backfield, averaging an impressive 6.0 yards per carry in the Week 1 win. The superstar running back remains locked in as a reliable RB1 ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

news.body: De’Von Achane (knee) suffered a season ending torn ACL against the Chiefs.
news.head: De’Von Achane (knee) suffers season-ending torn ACL
news.impact: Achane went down early in the Dolphins contest against Kansas City, with Ollie Gordon filling in as the primary rusher in his absence. Gordon is now a primary pickup for fantasy, and Jaylen Wright is worth a pickup as well.

news.body: Dolphins RB De'Von Achane has officially been ruled out for the remainder of Week 3 with a knee injury.
news.head: De'Von Achane (knee) ruled out
news.impact: Achane was tackled awkwardly in the first quarter and was taken to the locker room for further evaluation. Ollie Gordon will handle the primary running back duties for the remainder of the game against the Chiefs. He will finish the day with 17 yards on three carries.

news.body: De’Von Achane (knee) is questionable to return for the Miami Dolphins against the Kansas City Chiefs Sunday according to Ian Rapoport.
news.head: De’Von Achane (knee) questionable to return Sunday
news.impact: Achane suffered the knee injury early in the first quarter, rushing three times for 17 yards prior to exiting. Ollie Gordon II will take over in the backfield against the Chiefs Sunday.

news.body: De'Von Achane gained 74 yards on 20 carries and caught 3-of-6 targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
news.head: De'Von Achane grinds out 93 yards of offense in Week 2
news.impact: Achane's touches went up in Week 2, but his efficiency in the Dolphins' anemic offense was about the same. The dual-threat back has yet to find the end zone through two games while averaging just 3.5 yards per carry. He's best viewed as an RB2 for now, with his volume of touches being the main reason. Achane has a tough matchup coming against the Chiefs.

news.body: Emanuel Wilson ran for 81 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries in the Seahawks 30-23 win over the Chargers. He also caught 3-of-4 targets for 39 yards receiving and another score.
news.head: Emanuel Wilson scores twice Sunday
news.impact: After a fumble on a muffled punt by the Chargers early, Wilson took a screen pass from Sam Darnold to the house for the first score of the day. He was the clear workhorse in the first game since Jadarian Price was placed on IR.

news.body: Emanuel Wilson rushed nine times for 14 yards in the Seahawks’ 33-31 loss to the Washington Commanders in Week 3.
news.head: Emanuel Wilson quiet in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Wilson has struggled to make an impact out of the backfield to begin the season, recording less than 10 carries in two of three contests. The running back remains difficult to trust in a Seattle backfield with more questions than answers currently, with a Week 4 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.body: Emanuel Wilson ran 21 times for 92 yards and failed to catch his only target in Seattle's 31-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.head: Emanuel Wilson goes for 92 yards in win over Arizona
news.impact: Wilson led the Seahawks backfield in the big win, out-touching Jadarian Price on the ground 21 to 13. He's a speculative add at best as the Seahawks continue to rotate running backs.

news.body: Emanuel Wilson rushed the ball two times for three yards in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Emanuel Wilson uninvolved in win Wednesday
news.impact: There were many questions about Seattle's backfield split over the course of the offseason, and we finally got some answers on Wednesday. One of the takeaways is that Wilson is not likely to be a significant contributor in the rotation, as he saw just two out of the team's 20 RB rushing attempts on the night. It looks like Jadarian Price and George Holani have squarely established themselves as the top two backs on this team, with Wilson being a distant third.

news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 15 yards on nine carries in the Commanders loss to the Colts. He caught 2-of-4 passes for 35 yards.
news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt quiet in Week 4 loss
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt and the entire Commanders' rushing attack struggled to get anything going against the Colts. With the current quarterback situation in Washington, Croskey-Merritt and the rest of the running backs could be asked to see more work in a Week 5 matchup with the Giants.

news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 19 times for 36 yards while also hauling in his only target for seven yards in the Commanders’ 33-31 Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt bottled up in Week 3 win
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt has struggled to make an impact out of the backfield of late, rushing for less than 50 yards in each of the last two games. The running back remains a risky lineup option in all formats ahead of a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 43 yards on 12 carries and caught his lone target for five yards in the loss to Dallas Sunday.
news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt sees 12 carries in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt was out targeted by Rachaad White 6-to-1, but each tallied 43 yards on the ground. The Commanders' offense took a massive blow losing Jayden Daniels to a dislocated elbow, so the running game will likely be relied upon more heading into Week 3.

news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt carried the ball 16 times for 63 yards and one touchdown while also catching his only target for a loss of seven yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt reaches end zone in Week 1 loss
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt made the most of his opportunities out of the backfield, accounting for 50% of the carries for the Commanders in Week 1. The running back seems poised to receive as much volume as he can handle as the primary option out of the backfield to begin the season for head coach Dan Quinn, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.body: The Seahawks placed RB Jadarian Price on injured reserve.
news.head: Jadarian Price (chest) placed on IR
news.impact: Price aggravated a chest injury during Wednesday's practice. He will now miss at least four games. Emanuel Wilson and George Holani will lead the backfield with Zach Charbonnet returning as early as next week.

news.body: Jadarian Price has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
news.head: Jadarian Price (chest) ruled out Sunday
news.impact: Price was unable to practice this week due to a chest injury. Emanuel Wilson becomes a potential flex streamer this week.

news.body: Jadarian Price (chest) was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Jadarian Price (chest) downgraded to non-participant Thursday
news.impact: The rookie was limited at practice to start the week on Wednesday, but he has since been downgraded and was a non-participant on Thursday. He seems to be trending the wrong way for Week 4, and fantasy managers should expect George Holani (rib) to see a lot of work if Price is unable to play on Sunday.

news.body: Jadarian Price was limited in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Jadarian Price (chest) limited in practice Wednesday
news.impact: Price has fumbled each of the past two weeks with last week's turnover leading to him being benched for most of the first half. He is a risky RB2/flex play for now.

news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 46 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries, adding 31 yards on four catches in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs finds the end zone in Week 4
news.impact: Gibbs was limited to a season-low 77 yards of offense Sunday, but he still found the end zone for the seventh time in four weeks. The Panthers' defense did a solid job of holding Gibbs to 3.1 yards per carry and another season-low of four receptions. Still, the dynamic back remains an elite, dual-threat option heading to Arizona in Week 5.

news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 99 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries in a 31-24 win over the Jets. He caught 7-of-8 targets for 65 yards and a touchdown.
news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs tallies three touchdowns in Week 3 win
news.impact: Gibbs continues to impress this season, tallying six touchdowns in his first three games of the season. He caught an 11-yard pass in the fourth quarter to put the Lions on top of the Jets to seal the win. Gibbs and the Lions will take on the Panthers in Week 4.

news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed the ball 16 times for 52 yards and caught 6-of-8 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs plays well in loss Thursday
news.impact: Thursday's game wasn't great for Gibbs in terms of efficiency, but he was still able to accumulate over 100 yards and a touchdown on Thursday night, which left him with a great fantasy total in this shootout matchup against the Bills. He will continue to be a top-tier fantasy option at the RB position for the remainder of the season, provided he remains healthy for most of it.

news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs carried the ball 29 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns while also hauling in all five of his targets for 30 yards in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs leads backfield attack in Week 1 win over Saints
news.impact: Gibbs was dynamic out of the backfield for head coach Dan Campbell, averaging 5.4 yards per carry in the win. The running back remains an explosive RB1 option in all formats, with a Week 2 road matchup against the Buffalo Bills up next.

news.body: James Cook III rushed for 75 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in the loss to the Patriots. He caught both of his targets for eight yards.
news.head: James Cook III finds the end zone in Week 4
news.impact: Cook averaged 6.3 yards per carry on his 12 carries, providing the Bills with an incredibly efficient effort. Despite the strong performance, his 12 rushing attempts are a new season low. Cook and the Bills will take on the Rams in Week 5.

news.body: James Cook III carried the ball 24 times for 154 yards and one touchdown with one fumble lost in the Bills' 24-16 Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: James Cook III dominates on ground in Week 3 win over Chargers
news.impact: Cook III has been dynamic out of the backfield of late, rushing for over 130 yards with one touchdown in each of the last two contests. The running back remains an explosive RB1 option in all formats ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the New England Patriots.

news.body: James Cook III rushed the ball 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.head: James Cook III plays well in win Thursday
news.impact: Buffalo's offense was firing on all cylinders on Thursday night, and that included Cook. He rushed for 135 yards at an efficient clip of 6.5 yards per carry on the night and was able to get into the end zone on one of those carries. He wasn't very involved in the passing game, but he still dominated the backfield and was the only running back to receive even a single opportunity for the Bills.

news.body: James Cook III ran 13 times for 57 yards and caught three of four targets for 12 yards in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.head: James Cook III goes for 69 yards in big win over Texans
news.impact: Cook was fine on his touches and was saved by his three receptions in PPR formats, but it fantasy managers will be hoping for more. He’s still a premium running back, and he will get his chance early this week as the Bills play the Lions on Thursday night.

news.body: Javonte Williams ran for 62 yards on 19 carries with three touchdowns in the Cowboys 34-30 win over the Texans. He also caught 5-of-5 targets for 21 yards receiving.
news.head: Javonte Williams rushes for three touchdowns
news.impact: Williams didn't have the most efficient day on the ground, but he made up for it with three touchdowns and five receptions. He'll remain an RB1 play on Thursday against the Bucs.

news.body: Javonte Williams carried the ball 19 times for 98 yards and a touchdown while adding two catches for five yards in a 34-31 loss to the Ravens in Brazil in Week 3.
news.head: Javonte Williams finds the end zone in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Williams turned in another strong game on the ground for Dallas, finding the end zone on a two-yard run in the first quarter. The veteran tailback dominated the Dallas backfield, seeing all but six of the running-back carries. Williams has now rushed for 169 yards and two touchdowns while catching 10 passes for 56 yards and another touchdown through the air this season. He will be a solid RB1 in Week 4 against the Texans.

news.body: Javonte Williams rushed for 30 yards on 12 carries in the Cowboys 37-20 win over the Commanders. He caught 3-of-4 targets for 20 yards.
news.head: Javonte Williams sees 15 touches in Week 2
news.impact: Williams struggled to get anything consistent going against the Commanders' rush defense. Williams has logged 12 carries in both games this season, but has failed to get anything consistent going yardage wise. Williams and the Cowboys will take on the Ravens in Week 3.

news.body: Javonte Williams rushed the ball 12 times for 41 yards and a touchdown and caught five passes for 31 yards and another touchdown in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Javonte Williams scores twice in loss Sunday
news.impact: Williams was arguably Dallas' most impactful offensive player on Sunday night. He scored two touchdowns and totaled 72 yards on a night where the entire offense struggled, leaving him with a surprisingly good fantasy total on the week. He is clearly the team's bellcow running back at this point and should be viewed as a high quality fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Jaylen Warren rushed for 93 yards on 17 carries and caught 3-of-6 targets for 33 yards in Thursday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
news.head: Jaylen Warren gains 126 yards of offense Thursday night
news.impact: With backfield mate Rico Dowdle (toe) sidelined again, Warren took advantage of a workhorse load for the second straight game. He has yet to find the end zone this season, but Warren is averaging an elite 5.6 yards per carry while gaining over 300 yards on the ground through four games. He has also hauled in 13 of 19 targets for better than 35 yards per game. Warren is locked in as an RB2, especially in PPR formats.

news.body: Jaylen Warren rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries in a 30-27 win over the Bengals. He caught 3-of-4 targets for 49 yards.
news.head: Jaylen Warren excellent in Week 3 win
news.impact: Warren averaged 7.5 yards per carry and he dominated the rushing attempts with Rico Dowdle (toe) inactive Sunday. With the Steelers taking on the Browns on Thursday, Warren could be in line for a similar workload if Dowdle is unable to play.

news.body: Steelers RB Jaylen Warren (shoulder) is officially active for a Week 3 matchup with the Bengals.
news.head: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) officially active for Week 3
news.impact: Warren was limited in practice throughout the week but will play and start against the Bengals. With Rico Dowdle (toe) inactive, Warren could be in line for a workhorse role in Week 3.

news.body: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) is expected to play on Sunday against the Bengals after being listed with a shoulder injury this week. He was able to get some limited practice sessions in later in the week, and is likely good to go.
news.head: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) expected to play against Cincy
news.impact: Fellow RB Rico Dowdle is out for the game, so Warren’s availability is crucial for the team that lacks an experienced back behind him. He should be an RB2 with upside thanks to his pass catching skillset.

news.body: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love was dealing with an ankle injury on Sunday.
news.head: Jeremiyah Love dealt with ankle injury Sunday
news.impact: LaFleur clarified that Love's discomfort in Sunday's game is not the same ankle from the sprain he suffered in the preseason. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week.

news.body: Jeremiyah Love rushed the ball 14 times for 63 yards and caught one pass for -8 yards in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Jeremiyah Love underwhelming in loss Sunday
news.impact: The rookie didn't put up a good game on Sunday, netting just 55 total yards in the team's loss to the Giants. He is apparently dealing with some bumps and bruises of some kind and didn't see many touches in the second half as a result. Fantasy managers should keep close tabs on updates about his health throughout this next week of practice.

news.body: Jeremiyah Love ran for 90 yards on 21 carries in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday. He also caught 5-of-5 targets for 19 yards receiving and a touchdown.
news.head: Jeremiyah Love has career day Sunday
news.impact: Love totaled a career-high 26 touches. It was the first game so far where he clearly out-snapped Tyler Allgeier. He'll look to continue the workhorse role into next week against the Giants.

news.body: Jeremiyah Love ran nine times for 29 yards and caught three passes for 16 yards in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to Seattle.
news.head: Jeremiyah Love struggles in loss to Seattle
news.impact: Like the rest of the Cardinals' offense, Love struggled to move the ball against the Seahawks' stout defense. He will face yet another tough matchup next week, as Arizona takes on San Francisco.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins rushed 11 times for 40 yards, while RJ Harvey had seven carries for 25 yards in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Harvey also caught 10 passes for 68 yards out of the backfield.
news.head: J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey struggle in loss Sunday
news.impact: Denver couldn't get much going on the ground, with Dobbins and Harvey combining for just 65 rushing yards. Dobbins, however, continued to handle more of the rushing work. Harvey, meanwhile, was much more involved as a receiver and ended up leading the Broncos' offense in both receptions and receiving yards. The backfield remains a split, with Dobbins having the better chance at early-down work and Harvey carrying more upside in the passing game.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the 49ers.
news.head: J.K. Dobbins (hip) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Dobbins will remain a touchdown dependent low-end RB2 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins is practicing in full for Week 4 against the 49ers.
news.head: J.K. Dobbins (hip) practicing in full for Week 4
news.impact: Dobbins will remain in his lead role in the Broncos backfield.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins rushed the ball 17 times for 49 yards and caught 1-of-2 passes for four yards in Sunday night's 30-26 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: J.K. Dobbins leads team in rushing Sunday
news.impact: Dobbins saw the vast majority of carries out of the backfield on Sunday night, but he wasn't able to make much out of them, finishing with just 49 rushing yards in a narrow win over the Rams. He will likely maintain a large workload moving forward, however, especially now that rookie Jonah Coleman (ankle) has been placed on injured reserve.

news.body: Jonathan Taylor rushed for 95 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries in the win over the Commanders. He caught 1-of-4 targets for two yards.
news.head: Jonathan Taylor finds the end zone twice in Week 4 win
news.impact: Taylor found the end zone on a pair of five-yard touchdown runs in the second and third quarter. Taylor's strong 2026 season continues, as he has three multi-touchdown games in the team's first four games. Taylor and the Colts will take on the Steelers in Week 5.

news.body: Jonathan Taylor rushed for 68 yards on 23 carries in a 19-17 win over Houston. He caught 2-of-3 targets for four yards.
news.head: Jonathan Taylor held in check in Week 3 win
news.impact: Taylor continues to receive plenty of touches in the Colts' offense this season, but struggled to make the most of them in Week 3. His 72 total yards are a season low for Taylor. He will look to bounce back against the Commanders in Week 4.

news.body: Jonathan Taylor rushed the ball 24 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns while adding four receptions for 40 yards through the air in Sunday night's 33-30 OT loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Jonathan Taylor scores twice in overtime loss Sunday
news.impact: Taylor was the engine for Indianapolis' offense on Sunday night. He totaled 132 yards over the course of the night and was able to score two touchdowns on the ground. He has been very strong to start the season and should continue to be considered an elite fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Jonathan Taylor carried the ball 19 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns while also catching three of his four targets for 23 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.head: Jonathan Taylor rushes for two touchdowns in Week 1 loss
news.impact: Taylor was the lone bright spot in an underwhelming Colts offense to begin the season, averaging 5.2 yards per carry in the loss. The superstar running back will look to remain an impactful backfield option in Week 2 against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.body: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs had his initial court appearance moved up to Sept. 10 from Nov. 17 regarding Jacobs' misdemeanor charges.
news.head: Josh Jacobs has court appearance date moved up
news.impact: Jacobs was charged with battery and criminal destruction of property and is scheduled to appear at the Brown County courthouse on Sept. 10, multiple days before Green Bay's season opener against Minnesota. It is unclear how this will affect his return timeline; Jacobs is currently on the commissioner's exempt list, with a potential suspension looming.

news.body: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst said he expected Josh Jacobs to play for the team in 2026.
news.head: Josh Jacobs expected to play for Packers in 2026 per GM
news.impact: Gutekunst said he wants to let the process play out when asked if there’s a scenario in which the Packers release Jacobs. He was placed on the Commissioners Exempt List on Sunday. This will remain a situation to monitor.

news.body: Josh Jacobs has been placed on the commissioner exempt list by the National Football League according to Tom Pelissero.
news.head: Josh Jacobs placed on commissioner of exempt list
news.impact: Jacobs is now ineligible to practice or play for the Packers while the league continues their investigation into alleged improper behavior while being charged with two misdemeanors related to his conduct earlier in the week. If the running back is forced to sit out for any period of the regular season, MarShawn Lloyd will be in line to receive the majority of backfield work while the recently acquired Kaleb Johnson gets up to speed on the offensive playbook with Week 1 approaching.

news.body: Josh Jacobs has been charged with two misdemeanors following an incident in May. His initial court date is set for mid-November. The NFL is conducting its own investigation, and a suspension could soon follow.
news.head: Josh Jacobs charged with two misdemeanors stemming from May incident
news.impact: It's important to remember that the NFL has the ability to either suspend Jacobs at the start of the season or wait until the legal process is over. If they wait, then Jacobs will likely not face suspension until next year. If not, we could be looking at a potential 6-8 game absence, though that is more of an educated guess at this point. For anyone taking Jacobs in drafts right now, Marshawn Lloyd is a must-have handcuff and is a great target for Zero-RB builds.

news.body: Keaton Mitchell ran for 39 yards on 10 carries in the Chargers 30-23 loss against the Seahawks. He also caught 5-of-6 targets for 24 yards receiving.
news.head: Keaton Mitchell sees 10 carries Sunday
news.impact: Mitchell saw a team-high 10 carries on the day and 15 touches in total. It was a committee between him, Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal on Sunday.

news.body: Keaton Mitchell (ankle) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Keaton Mitchell (ankle) without injury designation for Sunday
news.impact: The veteran is going to be good to go on Sunday, despite being listed on the injury report throughout the week due to an ankle issue. He will continue to play second fiddle behind Omarion Hampton on this offense, although his exact snap share remains worth keeping an eye on this week.

news.body: Keaton Mitchell (ankle) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: Keaton Mitchell (ankle) limited again Thursday
news.impact: Mitchell was again a limited participant on Thursday due to the ankle injury that he's dealing with. It could leave him sidelined this week, in which case Kimani Vidal would be primed for more work in his absence.

news.body: Keaton Mitchell was wearing a walking boot on his left foot after practice.
news.head: Keaton Mitchell in walking boot
news.impact: Mitchell was listed as a limited participant in practice on Wednesday. His status will need to be monitored in practice the rest of the week.

news.body: Kendre Miller rushed the ball six times for just nine yards and lost a fumble in Monday night's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: Kendre Miller struggles in loss Monday
news.impact: Miller had a bad game on Monday night. He totaled just 19 yards on the ground and through the air against the Falcons, and he also lost a costly fumble, which further hurt his fantasy total. He should not be started in any fantasy league formats moving forward, especially with Alvin Kamara still seeing the bulk of the work in New Orleans' backfield right now.

news.body: Kendre Miller ran for 14 yards on four carries in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday. He also caught 2-of-3 targets for five yards receiving.
news.head: Kendre Miller sees four carries Sunday
news.impact: Miller saw some opportunity with Travis Etienne Jr. exiting early. Alvin Kamara was still the lead back in that span.

news.body: Kendre Miller was back at practice on Friday.
news.head: Kendre Miller (illness) returns to practice Friday
news.impact: Miller had been absent due to an illness. He'll need to be monitored when the injury report is released.

news.body: Kendre Miller (illness) was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Kendre Miller (illness) downgraded to non-participant Thursday
news.impact: Miller is a new addition to New Orleans' injury report. He's dealing with some kind of an illness right now and wasn't able to practice on Thursday as a result. He's likely day-to-day for the time being, but of he's cleared to play on Sunday and Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) isn't, he will be primed for more work than usual against the Raiders.

news.body: Kenneth Walker III carried the ball 22 times for 177 yards and two touchdowns while catching his lone target for a two-yard gain in a 30-27 win over the Raiders in Week 4.
news.head: Kenneth Walker III runs for 177 yards, two TDs in Week 4
news.impact: Walker notched his third multi-touchdown game of the season in what has been an impressive start to the year. The veteran running back found the end zone on rushes of two and 22 yards in the win. Overall, Walker has 537 rushing yards and six all-purpose touchdowns on the year. A locked-in high-end RB1 the rest of the way, he will be on bye in Week 5 before taking on the Chargers in Week 6.

news.body: Kenneth Walker III carried the ball 18 times for 70 yards and one touchdown while also catching both of his targets for three yards and one touchdown in the Chiefs' 24-10 Week 3 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Kenneth Walker III reaches end zone twice in Week 3 win over Dolphins
news.impact: Walker III has gotten off to an impactful start to the season out of the Kansas City backfield, recording multiple touchdowns in two of the first three contests. The running back remains a dynamic option as part of a revamped Chiefs offensive attack for head coach Andy Reid, with a Week 4 divisional matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders up next.

news.body: Kenneth Walker III rushed the ball 24 times for 117 yards and caught 6-of-10 targets for 61 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Kenneth Walker III totals 178 yards in OT win Sunday
news.impact: Walker's hot start to the season continued on Sunday night. He totaled 178 yards from scrimmage in a big win over the Colts, and he was able to do that while maintaining terrific efficiency. He will continue to be a top-tier fantasy asset for as long as he remains healthy and on the field moving forward.

news.body: Kenneth Walker III rushed the ball 23 times for 173 yards and a touchdown while catching 3-of-6 targets for 18 yards and an additional touchdown in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Kenneth Walker III dominant in win Monday
news.impact: Walker was absolutely dominant in his debut with the Chiefs on Monday night. He totaled 191 yards and two touchdowns over the course of the game, which was especially impressive considering that he did it against one of the best defenses in the NFL in the Broncos. He looks great on his new offense and should be in line for a huge season if he can stay healthy with this increased workload.

news.body: Kenny Gainwell carried the ball three times for five yards and caught both of his targets for 22 yards and a touchdown in a 17-14 loss to the Packers in Week 4.
news.head: Kenny Gainwell catches TD in Week 4
news.impact: Gainwell found the end zone on a 10-yard pass from Jalon Daniels in the fourth quarter. It has been a quiet season thus far for Gainwell, who has just 26 rushing yards and eight catches for 44 yards through four games. He will be a low-end flex option in Week 5 vs. the Cowboys.

news.body: Kenny Gainwell ran for -4 yards on three carries in the Buccaneers 23-16 loss against the Vikings on Sunday. He also caught 2-of-5 targets for 14 yards receiving.
news.head: Kenny Gainwell quiet again Sunday
news.impact: Gainwell was once again not involved much. It is worth noting Bucky Irving was on the sideline for most of the final quarter. The status of Irving will need to be monitored this week.

news.body: Kenny Gainwell ran for 10 yards on two carries in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns. He also caught 3-of-4 targets for five yards receiving.
news.head: Kenny Gainwell remains in limited role Sunday
news.impact: Bucky Irving was the clear lead back for the second straight week. Gainwell remains a pure stash for fantasy managers in his current role.

news.body: Kenny Gainwell ran for 15 yards on five carries in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught his line target for three yards receiving.
news.head: Kenny Gainwell uninvolved Sunday
news.impact: This felt like the perfect time for Gainwell to make an impact with Tampa Bay falling behind 21-3 early, but it was Bucky Irving in the passing game out of the backfield who caught seven passes. Gainwell is a risky flex play for now in PPR leagues until we see him more involved.

news.body: Bears head coach Ben Johnson said RB Kyle Monangai is day-to-day with his thumb injury.
news.head: Kyle Monangai (thumb) day-to-day
news.impact: Monangai is coming off a huge performance in Sunday's win over the Jets. His status will need to be monitored in practice throughout the week.

news.body: Kyle Monangai (thumb) will be evaluated for a thumb injury on Monday.
news.head: Kyle Monangai (thumb) to be evaluated Monday
news.impact: According to the running back, he looked down at his hand before realizing any pain. His status is up in the air, so fantasy managers will need to monitor the situation as details emerge on whether he will miss time.

news.body: Kyle Monangai carried the ball 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns while catching his lone target for four yards in a 23-12 win over the Jets in Week 4.
news.head: Kyle Monangai runs for 146 yards, two TDs in Week 4 win
news.impact: Monangai dominated D'Andre Swift in the game as Swift lost a costly fumble and saw his playing time cut afterwards. Monangai rushed for touchdowns of one and five yards in the win. He will continue to split carries with Swift but it might be more of an even split after his Week 4 performance. He's on the flex radar in fantasy heading into Week 5 against the Packers.

news.body: Kyle Monangai carried the ball 10 times for 31 yards in a 27-7 win over the Eagles in Week 3's Monday night game.
news.head: Kyle Monangai rushes for 31 yards in Week 3 win
news.impact: Monangai mixed in behind starter D'Andre Swift. He was held to 3.1 yards per carry by the Philadelphia defense in the contest while failing to find the end zone for the second straight game. Monangai will continue to see a modest workload for the Bears but he won't be a very strong fantasy option unless Swift were forced to miss time. He will now prepare to take on the Jets in Week 4.

news.body: Kyren Williams rushed the ball 16 times for 80 yards and two touchdowns and caught 10-of-13 targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Kyren Williams dominant in win Sunday
news.impact: Williams had a stellar game in Week 4. He led team with 80 rushing yards, found the end zone two different times, and caught ten passes for 67 yards through the air in Sunday's win over the Eagles. Fantasy managers should be well pleased with this performance and with the fact that he has entirely pulled ahead of Blake Corum in terms of touches in close matchups.

news.body: Kyren Williams rushed the ball 15 times for 88 yards and caught 6-of-7 targets for 70 yards in Sunday night's 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Kyren Williams stellar in loss Sunday
news.impact: Williams had a great showing on Sunday night. He was the team's leading rusher and maintained great efficiency at 5.9 yards per carry, and he was also very involved in the passing game with six catches for 70 yards over the course of the night. He will likely continue to serve as the team's RB1 for the foreseeable future, even more so in close matchups like this one was.

news.body: Kyren Williams rushed the ball 12 times for 85 yards and caught two passes for 12 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.head: Kyren Williams finds end zone Monday
news.impact: Williams had a productive night on Monday. He led the team in rushing and fell just three yards shy of the 100-total yards mark over the course of the game, and he was also able to haul in a touchdown to put the cherry on top. Concerns still exist for his season-long outlook, though, with Blake Corum seeing just one less touch on the night and seemingly only getting better and better.

news.body: Kyren Williams ran 11 times for 41 yards and the Rams' only touchdown. He also caught all three of his targets for 24 receiving yards.
news.head: Kyren Williams punches in score in loss to Niners
news.impact: Williams' day was saved by the touchdown; otherwise it was fairly miserable. Blake Corum showed out in his opportunities, but he was limited to ground work only. Kyren appears to be in a committee now, but he at least has the edge in passing situations, giving him more appeal.

news.body: MarShawn Lloyd carried the ball seven times for 13 yards and caught all five of his targets for 36 yards in a 17-14 win over Tampa Bay in Week 4.
news.head: MarShawn Lloyd catches five passes in Week 4
news.impact: Lloyd struggled on the ground but he did some damage via the passing attack in the close win. The Packers continued with their three-man attack in the backfield with Kaleb Johnson getting eight carries and Chris Brooks four. No one has been able to find success running the ball in Green Bay this season, however. Lloyd will be a low-end flex option heading into Week 5 against the Bears.

news.body: MarShawn Lloyd ran four times for 11 yards and caught two of three targets for seven yards in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons.
news.head: MarShawn Lloyd snags two passes in loss
news.impact: Lloyd wasn't all that impressive in this game, but he was better than Kaleb Johnson this time out. The backfield is a mess right now with Josh Jacobs out, and everyone is struggling to run. Expect both Lloyd and Johnson to be irrelevant for fantasy moe often than not.

news.body: MarShawn Lloyd rushed six times for 20 yards while also hauling in both of his targets for six yards and one touchdown in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.head: MarShawn Lloyd catches touchdown in quiet Week 2 performance
news.impact: Lloyd has underwhelmed despite increased touches out of the Green Bay backfield to begin the season, finishing with less than 40 rushing yards in each of the first two games. The running back remains a risky option as part of a running back group leaving a lot to be desired, with a Week 3 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.body: MarShawn Lloyd ran for 37 yards on 13 carries in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings. He did not catch his lone target.
news.head: MarShawn Lloyd sees 13 carries Sunday
news.impact: Lloyd was the lead back in the Packers backfield without Josh Jacobs. He was very inefficient as he averaged less than three yards per carry. He'll be a flex play next week against the Jets.

news.body: Mike Washington Jr. carried the ball nine times for 18 yards and lost a yard on his lone catch in a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs in Week 4.
news.head: Mike Washington Jr. runs for 18 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Washington couldn't replicate his big game in Week 3, where he ran for 54 yards and a touchdown on just five carries. The rookie runner remains a solid fantasy handcuff in all leagues in case something happens to Ashton Jeanty. Washington will face the Patriots in Week 5.

news.body: Mike Washington Jr. ran for 54 yards and a touchdown on five carries in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints on Sunday.
news.head: Mike Washington Jr. finds the end zone Sunday
news.impact: Washington found the end zone on an impressive run. He remains the clear backup behind Ashton Jeanty in the Raiders backfield.

news.body: Mike Washington Jr. rushed the ball three times for seven yards and failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Mike Washington Jr. uninvolved in loss Sunday
news.impact: Washington saw a decrease in opportunities on Sunday, falling to just three touches after having seven in the season opener a week ago. He isn't a big part of this offense right now and shouldn't be rostered in most league formats for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Mike Washington Jr. carried the ball seven times for 41 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Mike Washington Jr. sees seven touches in Week 1 win
news.impact: Washington Jr. was impactful operating behind Ashton Jeanty in the Las Vegas backfield, averaging 5.9 yards per carry in the win. The running back will look to continue to offer impactful touches as the primary handcuff to Jeanty in the Las Vegas backfield moving forward, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.body: Ollie Gordon II rushed the ball nine times for 100 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Ollie Gordon II plays well in loss Sunday
news.impact: Gordon was one of the only bright spots for Miami's offense this week. He finished with 100 yards and a touchdown on just nine carries, which left him with a great efficiency number in this game. He has clearly separated himself from Jaylen Wright in terms of talent and output, but they continue to be somewhat close together in terms of opportunities, which could limit Gordon moving forward.

news.body: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said all running backs on the roster are “going to have their roles.”
news.head: Ollie Gordon II: All RBs on Dolphins 'are going to have their roles'
news.impact: Gordon remains the most likely player to lead the backfield, but Jaylen Wright will figure to have a role when he is healthy. Gordon can be viewed as a borderline RB2 for now.

news.body: Ollie Gordon II carried the ball 17 times for 41 yards and one touchdown while also hauling in all three of his targets for 14 yards in the Dolphins' 24-10 Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Ollie Gordon II reaches end zone in Week 3 loss to Chiefs
news.impact: Gordon II took advantage of increased touches with De'Von Achane (knee) exiting early for head coach Jeff Hafley, posting more than three touches for the first time in three contests Sunday. The running back is in line to take over a No. 1 running back role with Achane expected to be sidelined for a significant amount of time according to Hafley, with a tough Week 4 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings up next.

news.body: Dolphins RB Ollie Gordon II (cramping) is questionable to return Sunday.
news.head: Ollie Gordon II (cramping) questionable to return
news.impact: Gordon jogged off to the locker room and is now officially questionable to return. This is a big blow to the Dolphins' offense with De'Von Achane (knee) already ruled out.

news.body: Omarion Hampton ran for 45 yards and a touchdown on nine carries in the Chargers 30-23 loss against the Seahawks. He also caught 2-of-2 targets for eight yards receiving.
news.head: Omarion Hampton finds the end zone Sunday
news.impact: Hampton saw just nine carries to 15 combined carries between Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. Hampton is a touchdown dependent flex play moving forward.

news.body: Omarion Hampton carried the ball 15 times for 56 yards while also failing to catch his lone target in the Chargers' 24-16 Week 3 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Omarion Hampton leads ground attack in Week 3 loss to Bills
news.impact: Hampton struggled to find consistent running room Sunday, rushing for less than 60 yards for the second time in the first three contests. The running back remains one of the more reliable options as part of an inconsistent Chargers offense to begin the season, with a Week 4 contest against the Seattle Seahawks up next.

news.body: Omarion Hampton rushed the ball 23 times for 94 yards and a touchdown and caught two passes for 21 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.head: Omarion Hampton scores once in loss Sunday
news.impact: Hampton was one of the lone bright spots for the Chargers on Sunday. He logged 115 total yards and found the end zone once over the course of the afternoon, though he left something to be desired in the passing game. He should continue to be a good fantasy option moving forward, though the present struggles of Los Angeles' offense may cap his upside from a fantasy perspective.

news.body: Omarion Hampton rushed for 43 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.head: Omarion Hampton finds the end zone in Week 1 loss
news.impact: A first-round pick in 2025, Hampton carried quite a bit of hype coming into his second NFL season, as did the Chargers' offense as a whole. At least some of that hype immediately died down after a disappointing season debut against a suspect Arizona defense, but it is only one game under new OC Mike McDaniel. Hampton found the end zone on an eight-yard run in the opening quarter, and this Chargers' attack will find its footing at some point. The Raiders are up next.

news.body: Quinshon Judkins rushed for 53 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries, adding 43 yards on six receptions in Thursday's 27-24 win over the Steelers.
news.head: Quinshon Judkins finds the end zone for the first time this season
news.impact: Judkins finally hit paydirt this season, plunging into the end zone from two yards out during the second quarter of Thursday's game. Judkins still averaged just over 3.0 yards per carry in this contest, but he totaled a season-high 96 yards of offense on 23 touches. After rushing for only 54 yards over the first two weeks, the second-year back has gained 123 yards over the last two.

news.body: Quinshon Judkins rushed the ball 18 times for 70 yards and caught two passes for nine yards in Sunday's 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.head: Quinshon Judkins underwhelming in win Sunday
